issue_context.body:

  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
My network setup is causing lots of unknown/bad MAC addresses to appear in the Unifi controller, which then adds them as entities in Home Assistant via the Unifi integration. I can remove these from the Unifi controller using the "Forget" option under known devices; however, this does not remove them from Home Assistant.  Looking through the integration code, I only see methods for adding new clients, but nothing removes clients that are removed from the controller.

These are causing the entities registry to be flooded (~1800 entities / month) and slowing down the system. The only way to remove these in bulk is to remove the Unifi integration and re-add it after clearing out the devices from the Controller.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: v0.106.0
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): n/a 
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Hass.io
- Integration causing this issue: Unifi
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/unifi/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`

  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->


Should be done within a few days

review_comments:
I think we can make this simpler by signaling each entity to remove itself instead of signaling these callbacks outside the entities. The entity knows its client mac address and knows what features the entity supports, wired or not etc.

If we would change this generally, we could also avoid storing the entity in `tracked` and instead just store the mac addresses in a set.

Generally we prefer to use the entity api from inside the entity.
I think it leads to double book keeping, right now its a single source of truth and control. You would still need to manage the set of tracked items and update it when Mac_addresses are removed
It's still a single source of truth. The signaller decides what should happen. The entity takes care of what is its responsibility, nothing more.
You mean the tracked set should be passed into all entities?

That works, but if we want to avoid making the entities responsible directly for `tracked` we can pass them a callback that they should call when they remove themselves. This callback would handle modifying `tracked`.

I imagine we create signals using the mac addresses. The entities register to listen for their own mac address. The entity has access to the controller and the client and the entity knows its type. So the check if it's time to remove an entity can be moved to each entity class. The entity can store a cached controller option as an instance attribute and compare that with the updated controller option when receiving the signal.
Ok, I will give it a shot
